0.description: Small (median ~850 students), mostly private, thin resources (~$7.8K instructional spend per FTE). Serve the highest-need students outside the large-access sector (median 48% Pell) with the weakest outcomes in the selective sector: 64% retention, 39% graduation.
0.label: Small access colleges

1.description: Big, open-door, majority-public systems (median ~4,100 students, 85% admission rate, 18:1 student-faculty ratio). The access workhorses: median 55% Pell, 52% graduation — scale on a budget.
1.label: Large access-serving institutions

2.description: The broad center of American four-year higher ed (n=1,028): mid-size comprehensives and private colleges, 82% admission, 30% Pell, 58% graduation. UNC Wilmington and Trine University both land here.
2.label: The mainstream middle

3.description: The resource-rich tier: 39% admission rate, ~$22.2K instructional spend per FTE, 9:1 student-faculty ratio, 91% retention, 84% graduation, 17% Pell. Harvard sits here — alongside Lehigh, Brandeis and Clark.
3.label: Selective and well-resourced

note: Editorial labels assigned after inspecting outputs/cluster_profiles.csv (fall 2022 cross-section, k-means k=4). The clustering script itself is label-free; labels live here so they can be debated without touching the analysis.
